ordered_diagnoses: Anorectal cancer with pelvic lymph node involvement

facts.raw_span: A 48-year-old man
12-year history of perianal fistula
recent mucinous discharge, pain, and perianal induration
incision and drainage of a recurrent perianal abscess
two indurated, ulcerative lesions each 7 cm in diameter
three external fistula openings around the anus
no inguinal lymphadenopathy
Upper endoscopy was unremarkable
internal fistula opening at the right side of the dentate line
otherwise normal mucosa in the rectum and colon
well-defined mass at the level of the anorectal junction extending into the right ischiorectal fossa
Histological examination of a biopsy specimen from the indurated area revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma

concepts.why: The presence of a well-defined mass at the anorectal junction with mucinous adenocarcinoma on histological examination supports this diagnosis.

aliases: Adenocarcinoma of the rectum with fistula
concepts.why: The combination of indurated lesions, external fistula openings, and an internal fistula opening at the dentate line, along with a mass at the anorectal junction, suggests this diagnosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Anorectal cancer with pelvic lymph node involvement
aliases: Cancer of the anorectum with pelvic lymph node metastasis
concepts.why: The presence of a well-defined mass at the anorectal junction with mucinous adenocarcinoma and enlarged pelvic lymph nodes supports this diagnosis.

rationales.F05: Large ulcerative lesions are highly suggestive of anorectal cancer.
rationales.F06: Multiple external fistula openings are common in rectal adenocarcinoma with fistula.
rationales.F09: Internal fistula opening is a characteristic feature of anorectal cancer.
rationales.F11: A well-defined mass at the anorectal junction is indicative of anorectal cancer.
rationales.F12: Histological examination revealing mucinous adenocarcinoma is diagnostic of anorectal mucinous adenocarcinoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: Histological examination revealed mucinous adenocarcinoma, which directly supports Anorectal mucinous adenocarcinoma, and the presence of a well-defined mass and internal fistula opening also align with this diagnosis.
